title: Drill record
description: The drill record, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #82: the rehearsal evidence for the ingress posture case's kill path. Each row names the kill path it rehearsed (the case must declare it — the two documents describe one platform), the day it was drilled (a real date, on or before the injected clock — a rehearsal recorded in the future is a rehearsal that has not happened), and the evidence that says so. The staleness clock is declared here, next to the evidence it judges: maxStalenessDays, 180 by default. The gate joins this record against the posture case — a kill path declared but never rehearsed fails, and a rehearsal older than the clock flags for review.

version.description: Version of the drill record. Rehearsals are versioned like the case they rehearse.

reviewedOn.description: Date the record was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags dates in the future — evidence cannot arrive before the work it evidences.

owner.description: The team that owns the rehearsals. A drill record with an owner and a review cadence is the discipline.

maxStalenessDays.description: The rehearsal staleness clock in days, default 180. A rehearsal older than the clock flags for review — a kill path rehearsed once and never again is a kill path that has drifted.

drills.description: The rehearsals on record. Empty is well-formed — and a declared kill path with an empty record is exactly the never-rehearsed finding.

killPath.description: The kill path this row rehearses. Must be declared in the posture case — a rehearsal of a kill path the case never declares is a rehearsal of a promise the platform never made.

drilledOn.description: The day the rehearsal ran, YYYY-MM-DD. Must not postdate the injected clock — a drill recorded in the future is a drill that has not happened, and it never softens the kill path's posture.

evidence.description: The cited evidence — the drill log, the runbook entry, the recording. A rehearsal without a record is a rumor.
